headline: Panel-level references reconcile hidden diversity in wheat and cereal genomes
label: Plant Genomic Reference Resources
summary: Single-genome references miss variation; panel-level pan-references and consistent repeat annotations now capture it across assemblies.
synthesis: The common thread is moving from single-genome references to panel-level representations that are reconciled or annotated consistently across assemblies. WheatPanRef builds a linear pan-reference for wheat from reconciled Chinese Spring assemblies plus non-CS sequences from 37 accessions. Earl Grey ParTEA constructs a shared non-redundant transposable element library across genome panels, enabling consistent comparative TE annotation from pangenomes to deep phylogenetic scopes. TideCluster takes a reference-independent route, clustering tandem repeat arrays into repeat family catalogs with consensus monomers for comparative and pangenomic analysis. The cereal pangene atlas, spanning about 500 gene families across four cereals, reports pangene membership rising 59-264% over single-genome analyses. What is new here is explicit reconciliation of diversity across panels rather than per-genome annotation.
